preamble: Unstressed [i] (and its lax counterpart [ɪ]) loses its front, high quality and becomes the central vowel [ə]. In the English weak vowel merger, unstressed [ɪ] in roses or Lenin merges with the schwa of Rosa's and Lennon in most accents outside traditional RP. Middle High German weakened all unstressed vowels of Old High German to ⟨e⟩ [ə], so the plural gesti 'guests' became geste.

examples.note: The from-form is the conservative pronunciation, kept in traditional RP. Unstressed [ɪ] merges with schwa in most Australian, New Zealand, North American and Irish accents and in 21st-century Southern British speech.
Unstressed vowels of Old High German were weakened to ⟨e⟩, pronounced [ə].
